newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU vets reject ban on suspect BSE sheep tissue.
newsitem.headline: EU vets reject ban on suspect BSE sheep tissue.

text.p: European Union veterinary officials on Tuesday rejected a Commission proposal to remove suspect tissue from sheep and goats as well as cattle, a Commission official said.

The proposal, a precautionary move following British and French research showing that sheep could catch mad cow disease, or Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), will now be sent to a meeting of EU farm ministers on December 16-17.
"The officials rejected a slightly amended text," the official said after a reconvened meeting of the EU's Standing Veterinary Committee of senior member state veterinary officials.
The proposal was rejected by 12 member states with only Britain and France voting in support and Ireland abstaining.

On Friday, the Commission delayed forcing a vote after many member states raised objections to the proposal, saying the measures were economically unjustified in view of the negligeable risk involved.
A previous Commission proposal to remove sheep brains, spleens and spinal cords from human and animal food was rejected by the committee in August.
